text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.
LONDON - British shares fell as fresh weakness hit Wall Street and government bonds dropped sharply. The FTSE 100 index lost 30.9 points to 4,308.3, capping a fall of 28.5 points since last Friday.

FRANKFURT - German DAX index fell 0.5 percent after a bout of profit-taking. Dealers see outlook stable at lower levels, but still see potential for more gains next week. The DAX index ended down 17.08 points at 3,259.64, but was up 75.55 for the week.
PARIS - French shares ended sharply lower, affected by another drop on Wall Street and profit-taking. The blue-chip CAC-40 index fell 21.85 points to 2,607.55. It rose 44.71 for the week.
ZURICH - Swiss shares closed down but above the day's lows in derivatives-driven trading. The All-share SPI fell 18.57 points to 2,851.56, but rose 19.62 on the week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks tumbled on profit-taking after the yen gained against the dollar in afternoon trading. The Nikkei 225 average lost 464.56 points to 18,557.00, a decline of 2.44 percent. It fell 477.54 for the week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended with heavy losses on Friday as comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan earlier this week returned to haunt the market. The Hang Seng Index tumbled 147.88 points, or 1.09 percent, to close at 13,398.72, capping a loss of 46.13 on the week.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended lower with investors still nervous before the weekend following the hawkish comments by Fed Chairman Greenspan. The All Ordinaries index ended 14.8 points lower at 2,449.9 and was down 25.4 from a week ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks fell, hurt by weakness on Wall Street overnight, profit-taking and nervousness over Thursday's money supply figures. The industrial index fell 79.4 points to 8,244.3, a drop of 135 from a week ago; the overall index shed 50.7 points to 7,145.3, but rose 21.2 points for the week, and the gold index lost 22.6 points to 1,565.5; it was up 47.7 from last Friday.
